title: No ISMS scope statement captured before audit creation — ISO 27001 Clause 4.3 requires defined scope
description:
Re-verified 2026-08-22 against `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/audit-assurance-2/CreateTemplateAuditPage.jsx` (full 1379-line read). The backend/service plumbing previously cited as the fix is real: ISMS-scope state is declared (lines 320-323), `upsertIsmsScope` is called non-blockingly after audit creation (lines 620-629), and the client service method correctly PUTs to `/audit-assurance/:id/isms-scope`, backed by a real `audit-isms-scope.model.js` + `isms-scope.routes.js` + controller on the backend. However, after reading the full file there is NO rendered input UI anywhere that ever calls `setIsmsOrgBoundary`, `setIsmsLocations`, `setIsmsServicesInScope`, or `setIsmsExclusions` — the only remaining trace of a UI section is a bare comment placeholder `{/* ── Section 6: ISMS Scope ── */}` at line 1328, immediately followed by the Actions bar. `hasIsms` is therefore always false in practice and `upsertIsmsScope` never fires with real data. From a user's perspective the ISMS scope statement is still never captured before/during audit creation — the previously recorded 'fixed' status overclaimed a backend-only, functionally-inert wiring as a full fix.

Claude Fix Prompt:
```
Fix D-03 in vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/audit-assurance-2/CreateTemplateAuditPage.jsx.

The backend isms-scope upsert plumbing already exists (state at lines 320-323, upsertIsmsScope call at 620-629) but there is no input form — replace the dead placeholder comment near line 1328 with a real "ISMS Scope" section: org boundary textarea, locations multi-input, services-in-scope textarea, exclusions textarea, each bound to the existing setIsmsOrgBoundary/setIsmsLocations/setIsmsServicesInScope/setIsmsExclusions setters so hasIsms actually becomes true when the user fills it in.
```

title: No audit objectives or audit criteria fields — ISO 19011 §5.4 requires both to be documented
description:
Files: `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/audit-assurance-2/CreateTemplateAuditPage.jsx`, `audit.model.js`

Re-verified 2026-08-22 by full read of CreateTemplateAuditPage.jsx: no UI field for objectives/criteria exists anywhere, and the `createAudit` payload sends only `name, description, type, priority, mode, templateId, startDate, dueDate, projectId, leadAuditor, secondaryAuditors` — no `auditObjective` or `auditScope`. The backend `audit.model.js` already has dedicated fields for exactly this (`auditObjective` string; `auditScope.clauses`/`auditScope.description`, explicitly commented "ISO 27001 Clause 9.2.2" / "Audit Report Fields") but the frontend never surfaces or sends them — confirms still open.

Claude Fix Prompt:
```
Fix D-04 in vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/audit-assurance-2/CreateTemplateAuditPage.jsx and audit.model.js.

ISO 19011 §5.4 requires audit objectives and criteria — neither field exists in the UI. Note: audit.model.js already has auditObjective and auditScope.clauses/description fields (unused, duplicated — see M-005); reuse those instead of adding new ones.

Required changes:
1. CreateTemplateAuditPage.jsx: add tag-input/textarea for each, wired to the existing auditObjective/auditScope model fields. Pre-populate auditCriteria with the selected framework name on Quick Template selection.
2. Required for certification type, optional for internal.
3. Display both prominently at the top of Audit Detail view.
```

title: `not_applicable` status requires no justification and creates no SoA entry — ISO 27001 Clause 6.1.3(c) requires documented exclusion reasons
statusRaw: 🔴 OPEN (flipped back from in_progress — core defect only half-fixed)
description:
Files: `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/audit-assurance-2/ScopeItemDetailDrawer.jsx`, `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/workflow/workflow.controller.js`, `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/audit-assurance/controllers/soa.controller.js`

Re-verified 2026-08-22 — partially fixed since last run. The 'requires no justification' half is now FALSE at the API layer: `workflow.controller.js` (lines 10-18) hard-rejects (400) any `audit_scope_item` → `not_applicable` transition unless `justificationText` is at least 10 characters, and persists it to `AuditScopeItem.notApplicableJustification` (lines 81-99). The 'creates no SoA entry' half REMAINS TRUE: the Statement of Applicability is a fully separate model/workflow (`models/audit-soa.model.js` + `controllers/soa.controller.js`) — an `AuditSoa` document is only created/updated via the explicit `POST /:auditId/soa/:scopeItemId` (`updateSoaControl`), which independently requires its own `exclusionReason` when `applicable:false` (lines 364-369, citing ISO 27001 §6.1.3(d) in its own error message). Nothing in the workflow transition (or anywhere else in the module) auto-creates or syncs an SoA row when a scope item becomes `not_applicable`; `_merge()` (soa.controller.js line 150) defaults `applicable: true` for any scope item with no existing SoA doc, so a scope item marked not-applicable on the audit side still shows as "Applicable" on the SoA side until someone manually re-enters the same decision on the separate SoA tab. No `approvedBy`/exclusion-reason-dropdown exists on the scope-item side either (only a single free-text `notApplicableJustification`).

**Re-verified 2026-08-30** after pulling the latest `vibrantix-backend`/`vibrantix-client-panel` (`feature/dev`): no `audit-assurance` files were touched by this pull (confirmed via `git diff --stat` on the fast-forwarded commits), so both halves are unchanged. Citation corrected: the justification-required half's real location is `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/workflow/workflow.controller.js:10-18,82-93` — the GENERIC cross-feature workflow engine's HTTP controller (shared with evidence/policy/vendor review transitions) — not `audit-assurance/controllers/workflow.controller.js`, which is a different file handling only audit-level draft/in_review/approved/archived transitions and has no `not_applicable`/`justificationText` logic at all. The SoA-sync half remains fully unaddressed — `workflow.controller.js`'s only post-transition side effects are a risk-webhook fire and a `notApplicableJustification` field write; no `AuditSoa` upsert exists anywhere in it.

**Status flipped 2026-08-30:** the defect's own title covers two requirements ('requires no justification' AND 'creates no SoA entry') — only the first is closed. Since the SoA-sync half (arguably the more consequential half, since it drives whether the Statement of Applicability itself is trustworthy) is completely unaddressed with no code progress, `in_progress` overstated the state; flipped back to `open`.

Claude Fix Prompt:
```
Fix the remaining gap for D-24: when a scope-item workflow transition to not_applicable succeeds in workflow.controller.js, also upsert the corresponding AuditSoa document (applicable:false, exclusionReason mirrored from justificationText) via the same code path soa.controller.js's updateSoaControl uses, so the SoA tab and the scope item never disagree about applicability.
```

Citation corrected from the original 608 to 716-717.

title: `deleteAudit()` hard-deletes scope items without checking open findings or CARs — orphaned records corrupt reports
description:
Files: `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/audit-assurance/audit-assurance.controller.js:819–834` (citation corrected from the original 598–612 due to file growth)

Re-verified 2026-08-22: `deleteAudit()` (current lines 819-834) still cascades only `AuditScopeItem.deleteMany({auditId})`, `AuditAssuranceChange.deleteMany({auditId})`, and `audit.deleteOne()` via `Promise.all` — no query against `AuditNonConformance` (the merged findings/CARs collection) exists before deletion. Orphaned finding/CAR documents still pointing at a deleted `auditId`/`scopeItemId` remain a live risk. Defect reproduces exactly as originally described.

Claude Fix Prompt:
```
Fix H-002 in vibrantix-backend/src/modules/audit-assurance/audit-assurance.controller.js lines 819–834.

deleteAudit() leaves orphaned findings and CARs in the merged audit_nonconformances collection.

Required changes:
1. Pre-delete check:
     const [openFindingsAndCars] = await Promise.all([
       AuditNonConformance.countDocuments({ auditId, deletedAt: null, status: { $nin: ['closed', 'cancelled', 'verified'] } }),
     ]);
2. If any exist, reject 422: "Cannot delete audit with open findings or corrective actions."
3. If permitted (draft only), use a transaction to soft-delete in order: scope items → audit_nonconformances rows → audit document.
4. Never hard-delete audit records that have associated findings/CARs.
```

title: Mixed soft-delete pattern: `audit_scope_items` uses both `isDeleted` AND `deletedAt`; `audit_findings` uses `isDeleted`; `audit_nonconformances` uses `deletedAt`; controllers filter inconsistently — deleted records leak
statusRaw: 🔴 OPEN (flipped back from in_progress — standardisation never completed)
description:
Files: `audit-scope-item.model.js` (isDeleted+deletedAt), `models/audit-finding.model.js` (isDeleted+deletedAt, now legacy/dead-write), `audit-nonconformance.model.js` (deletedAt only)

Re-verified 2026-08-22, architecture has shifted since last run (audit_findings and audit_nonconformances have been merged into one collection). Current state: `audit-nonconformance.model.js` is now fully standardized on `deletedAt`/`deletedBy` only (lines 155-156, query-exclusion middleware lines 195-202) — this part of the prior partial fix holds. `models/audit-finding.model.js` (the pre-merge model) still carries both `isDeleted` and `deletedAt` with sync-on-save middleware (lines 96-103) — but per `findings.controller.js`'s own code comments (lines 18-22) this model is no longer written to anywhere in the module (dead-write, retained read-only as a rollback safety net) and `controllers/programme.controller.js` is the one remaining live reader of it, meaning the Audit Programme report's findings summary is now silently stale (returns 0/empty going forward) — a new, related bug from the migration, not itself one of the tracked defect IDs. `audit-scope-item.model.js` still carries BOTH `isDeleted` and `deletedAt` with the same sync middleware (lines 357-359, 392-398) — this part of the original defect is unchanged and still open. Net: standardization is real for the merged NC/CAR collection but the scope-item model (and the now-orphaned legacy finding model) remain dual-field, so "in_progress" remains the accurate status.

**Re-verified 2026-08-30** after pulling the latest `vibrantix-backend` (`feature/dev`): confirmed via `git diff --stat` that no `audit-assurance` files were touched by this pull — all three findings above (audit-scope-item.model.js still dual-field; audit-nonconformance.model.js correctly deletedAt-only; audit-finding.model.js still dual-field, dead-write, still read by programme.controller.js) are unchanged and re-confirmed directly against the current code.

**Status flipped 2026-08-30:** the live-model standardisation (audit-nonconformance.model.js) happened as a side effect of an unrelated collection merge, not a targeted fix for this ID, and the two remaining dual-field/stale-read issues this defect actually tracks (audit-scope-item.model.js, programme.controller.js's stale AuditFinding reads) have seen zero code movement across every re-verification. `in_progress` was not warranted; flipped back to `open`.

Claude Fix Prompt:
```
Fix H-003 remaining scope: standardise audit-scope-item.model.js to deletedAt-only (it already has a pre-save sync hook keeping isDeleted in step, so this is a read-path cleanup — update all controller queries that check isDeleted directly to check deletedAt instead, then drop the isDeleted field in a follow-up migration). Separately, migrate controllers/programme.controller.js off the dead AuditFinding model onto AuditNonConformance (recordType:'finding') so its report data stops being silently stale.
```

title: Closure approve/reject protected by `audit.update` (too broad) — no `audit.approve` permission; any write-access user can approve their own closure
description:
Files: `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/audit-assurance/routes/audit-closure.routes.js:20–22` (citation corrected from the original 16–17 due to file growth)

Re-verified 2026-08-22: `/request-approval`, `/approve`, and `/reject` all still use `requirePermission('audit.update')`. This is confirmed still too broad — and notably, `audit.approve` DOES exist and is actively enforced elsewhere in this same module (`routes/governance.routes.js:45-48` gates report approve/reject/publish/archive with it), so there is no technical reason closure approval couldn't use the same permission — it simply wasn't wired up here. A partial mitigation exists that wasn't present in the original defect write-up: `audit-closure.service.js`'s `approveClosure()` (lines 142-144) now blocks the LITERAL same user who requested closure from approving it (`AppError.forbidden('Approver cannot be the same as the requestor')`). However, any other user merely holding the broad `audit.update` permission — not a dedicated approver/manager role — can still approve/reject, so the core role-separation gap remains.

Claude Fix Prompt:
```
Fix H-004 in vibrantix-backend/src/modules/audit-assurance/routes/audit-closure.routes.js lines 20-22.

Change requirePermission('audit.update') to requirePermission('audit.approve') on the /request-approval, /approve, and /reject routes — audit.approve already exists as a permission (see governance.routes.js) and just needs to be applied here too. Assign audit.approve only to Audit Manager and Admin roles — not Lead Auditor.
```

title: CAR evidence upload accepts any S3 key with no file-type allowlist, size limit, or bucket path constraint
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-22. `corrective-action.service.js` defines `ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS`/`ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES` sets and `MAX_EVIDENCE_BYTES = 25MB` (lines 24-34). `addEvidence()` (lines 461-514) validates the extension allowlist (482-487), constrains the S3 path to `evidence/${orgId}/` (490-492), and verifies real server-side size/MIME via S3 `HeadObject` (497-510) rather than trusting client-supplied metadata. `uploadEvidenceFile()` (lines 554-582) applies the same three checks for direct uploads. Confirmed fixed and more thorough than originally claimed. Citation corrected from the original 328-338.

title: Closure state transitions not enforced — `not_started → pending_approval` bypasses checklist; `rejected → approved` without rework cycle
description:
Files: `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/audit-assurance/services/audit-closure.service.js:47–203` (citation corrected from the original 52–202)

Re-verified 2026-08-22 — narrower than originally described. The `not_started → pending_approval` checklist-bypass half is NO LONGER TRUE: `requestApproval()` (lines 87-129) hard-blocks with a 400 unless `checklist.length > 0` and every item is completed, regardless of the closure's current status. The `rejected → approved` half REMAINS TRUE: `rejectClosure()` (lines 172-203) only flips `closureStatus`/`approval.status` to 'rejected' — nothing resets checklist completion or forces documented rework. `requestApproval()`'s only block is `approval.status === 'approved'` (line 106); 'rejected' passes straight through, so a requestor can immediately re-call `requestApproval()` (re-entering `pending_approval` with zero required rework) and then get approved, with no state machine enforcing that any rework actually happened or was documented.

Claude Fix Prompt:
```
Fix the remaining half of H-006 in audit-closure.service.js: requestApproval(). When called while closure.approval.status === 'rejected', require a new field (e.g. reworkNotes, min 20 chars) documenting what was changed since rejection before allowing re-entry to pending_approval, and store it on the closure record's history for the eventual approver to review.
```

title: Scope import error `console.error()`'d but not re-thrown — API returns `201 Created` with empty audit; user gets false success
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-22. `audit-assurance.controller.js`'s `createAudit()` (lines 294-332) wraps each import mode (`intelli_audit`, `requirements`, `template`) in a try/catch that logs via `logger.error(...)` (not `console.error`), rolls back by deleting the just-created audit document (`AuditAssurance.deleteOne({_id: audit._id})`), and returns `res.status(500).json({ error: 'Scope import failed', detail: err.message })` — never a silent fall-through to 201. Citation corrected from the original 188-230.

title: Cross-module evidence linkage is one-directional, and the alternate 'Attach Evidence' entry point is a non-functional stub that fakes a success toast
description:
Evidence attached from within an audit (attachEvidence, audit-assurance.controller.js:1163-1211) only writes to AuditScopeItem.evidenceAttachments - the Evidence model has no field referencing back to the audit/scope item, and evidence-management's components have no 'used in Audit X' cross-reference anywhere. Separately and more acutely: RequirementFullView.jsx renders EvidenceSection.jsx, whose 'Attach Evidence' modal calls auditV3Service.attachEvidenceToRequirement - a stub that does console.warn('...not available yet') and returns {success:false, message:'Feature not available yet'}. handleAttachEvidence in EvidenceSection.jsx never checks the returned success flag - it unconditionally shows a green 'Success - Evidence attached successfully' toast, closes the modal, and calls onUpdate(), even though nothing was persisted.

Auditor-facing breakage: an auditor using this page believes they have linked evidence to a requirement when the platform silently discarded the action - a genuinely deceptive UX.

title: Cannot distinguish "not yet reviewed" from "actively rejected" evidence
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27: `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/audit-assurance/controllers/evidence-status.controller.js:62-64` now computes three genuinely distinct counts per scope item — `approved = attachments.filter(a => a.verdict === 'approved').length`, `rejected = attachments.filter(a => a.verdict === 'rejected').length`, `pending = attachments.filter(a => a.verdict === null || a.verdict === undefined).length` — not conflated. `audit-report-generator-service/app/services/report_generation/evidence_status_aggregator.py:34-46` documents and consumes these as distinct `approved_count`/`rejected_count`/`pending_count` fields, with `coverage_status` distinguishing 'partial' (rejected>0) from 'uncovered' (no evidence) from 'covered'.
description:
**Files (original):** R10 Evidence Status aggregation path
**Root Cause (original):** Both 'not yet reviewed' and 'actively rejected' evidence were counted together as rejected, with no way to tell them apart.
**Status:** FIXED — see fixEvidence. Note: `pending_count` is still computed as a derived remainder (`ev_count - approved - rejected`) rather than an independent count in the Python aggregator (`evidence_status_aggregator.py:162`) — this is the previously-documented G-R10-02 concern (not itself tracked in this JSON store) and is low-risk since approved/rejected are now independently and correctly computed.
**Recategorized 2026-08-29:** Moved from evidence-management — this is squarely an Audit Assurance R10 Evidence Status defect (the fix itself lives in `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/audit-assurance/...`). Original ID/sourceFile preserved as historically documented.
